To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the main part of proton emission in the interaction of C-12 with C, Cu, Pb and Sn target nuclei at 36 AGeV is due to the decay of a moving source with the rapidity of about y = 1, and that the excitation energy of this source is about 1.5 GeV.

in the interactions of 12 C-ions at an energy of E = 3.6 A GeV with C, Cu, and Pb target nuclei, the main contribution to the proton inclusive spectra in the investigated kinematics is due to emission of particles from a moving source.
the proton emission in the interaction of carbon nuclei at 3,6 GeV/n with different target nuclei is dominated by emission from a moving, highly excited source.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the dynamics of the interaction of 3.7 GeV/nucleons with various target nuclei.
the investigation of the mechanism of formation of moving sources in collisions of 12 C nuclei with various target nuclides at 3.65 GeV/nucleonic energy.
a study of inclusive proton spectra in collisions of 12 C nuclei with C, Cu, and Pb nuclei at an energy of about 3.6 GeV/nucleon.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the source properties are independent of the colliding system and are governed by the projectile-target combination.
in all the studied interactions, the source of protons is formed at an early stage of the interaction and moves at a rapidity y = y t + Δ y.

the data obtained in the present study can be explained by the formation of a moving fireball, whose rapidity differs greatly from the rapidity of the effective fireballs in the collisions of carbon- and lead-ions with the same target nucleus, but the excitation energy is the same for all the systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the source is moving with the velocity of 0.5c.

in collisions of 12 C with various target nuclei the main contribution to the proton cross section is due to the emission from a moving, hot and compressed source with an excitation energy of ∼1.5 GeV and with a temperature of ∼20 MeV.
the source is formed in the interaction of two nuclei at the moment when the nuclei have just started to overlap.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proton emission from the moving source is the dominant mechanism for the formation of the proton spectra in the kinematic region under consideration.
a moving source of protons is formed in collisions of 12 C with C, Cu, and Sn target nuclei, which is not observed in collisions with a Pb target nucleus.
in collisions of carbon nuclei with heavy targets, a source is formed which moves in the direction opposite to the projectile motion.
